Reviews: Inception: Slightly Dazed and Totally Amazed
main_review: To my astonishment, Inception managed to surpass my greatest hopes. Watching it for the first time was one of the most profound movie experiences of my life.Action movies are supposed to take us on a roller-coaster ride. But rarely does a film take us on an intellectual roller-coaster ride. Rarely does the plot captivate us so thoroughly that we feel as if we are a young child experiencing the joy of movies for the first time. That's what Christopher Nolan attempts with Inception, and in my opinion, he's achieved his goal. It is a genuine mind trip.Inception is a surprisingly current movie, exploring what it means to live in the 21st century with different levels of reality.Inception is a meditation on the modern society where wealth and technology enable us to create our own dream worlds, escaping from reality. Every one of us lives in a world of the Internet. We play endless hours in make-believe virtual worlds through video games. We have almost unlimited access to movies and television that take us constantly into fiction. We interact with friends in virtual social networks. We have blogs which act as a sort of avatar, a representation of ourselves. We wear clothes that make us into made-up characters. We play and watch sports that simulate the drama and thrill of warfare. And we have created companies that are pseudo kingdoms, where business leaders act as modern-day royalty.

Here I'll be reviewing Inception, a movie I just re-watched for the 3rd time a short while ago. Inception was the 4th highest grossing film of 2010 and 14th highest rated movie ever (according to IMDb) and is well known for it's beautiful imagery and complex plot.
Inception follows Cobb (played by Leonardo DiCaprio), a man haunted by the death of his wife, who makes a living off of entering people's subconscious. When a wealthy man wants him to head into a young CEO's mind and subliminally make him break up his company Cobb assembles a team to do so. Little does he realize the further he goes into the CEO's subconscious the deeper he goes into his own. I think the actors did a brilliant job, from the big names of Leonardo DiCaprio (Titanic, Catch me if you can) and Michael Caine (The Batman Trilogy) to the lesser known ones like Ellen Page (who plays Ariadne).
What I really liked about this movie is it keeps you guessing. Just when you start to understand what's going on it changes things up. Its dream worlds are brilliantly imagined and it's plot is well thought-out with all of its intricacies. Some of the scenes were even done with practical effects. For the fight in the hallway with changing gravity, they actually built a hallway and spun it. My biggest gripe with the film is the dialogue which, while well written, is filled with exposition at the beginning of the film and slightly awkwardly cut occasionally. Though with this sort of film this is a necessary evil and did have action scenes to break it up.
I think the main target audience would be people who enjoy mind-bending thrillers and action movies aged (as the MPAA rating suggests) 13+. I give this movie a 9.5/10 and recommend it for anyone to see as it's one of the best of it's genre.

I'd like to keep my review rather to the point.Pros: 1. its theme - dream is a fascinating topic to say the least. There are a lot of unknowns in dreamworld. 2. its plot - there are several sweet twists and unpredictable turns. 3. its edgy drive - although you know what's coming next, still you feel jumpy about it when it does.4. its rapid storyline - the story moves fast from one scene to another, making the viewers feel like on a roller coaster ride. At times, it's hard to keep up, even after watching it several times. 5. its sophistication - there is a lot of information to remember and digest. This is the very thing the modern moviegoers are after, I believe. 6. its realism - okay, pun intended. The movie explains (or at least tries to) the ins and outs of what dream is about and how it functions, some of which are very familiar with and dear to us.Cons: 1. its poor character development - although the acting was convincing enough there was not enough of character development. I wonder how many people really felt connected to the main character(s) after watching the movie. Yes, the movie talks about emotional struggles but it was more of an action film than anything else, if you ask me. 2. too many distractions - I found that the movie had more characters than necessary. They may play certain roles in the plot but they seemed more of distractions than anything else. I wish the movie was more focused. 3. a bit preachy - I noticed that the characters would explain things about dreamworld and then the exact things happen later in the movie. I'm afraid, Inception overused this trick. In conclusion, its theme is fascinating but its delivery is not without room for improvement. I highly recommend you to go and read Somewhere carnal over 40 winks, if you dig this kind of flicks. YAaay!

Reviews: No, it is not overrated. This film is a masterpiece.
main_review: INCEPTION - 2010Directed by Christopher NolanStarring Leonardo DiCaprio, Ellen Page and Joseph Gordon-LevittPlot Overview: ​In a final attempt to see his kids once more, renowned Dream Thief Cobb(Leonardo DiCaprio) takes on an impossible task - plant an idea in someone's mind - or perform Inception. With the help of a new crew, Cobb must overcome his fears and delve deeper than anyone has done before.Don't come up to me and say this film is overrated because it really isn't. I don't believe it deserves a spot as one of the Greatest Movies of all Time, that is fair. But this movie is a masterpiece on every level. I have but ONE, minor flaw with this movie. Aside from that, it is one of the closest things to perfect in recent memory. I HIGHLY recommend you see this movie if you have not.The concept for this movie is amazing. It hurts my head to think about the logic of it but I'll be dammed if it isn't awesome. The story surrounding this concept is so well thought out and intricately designed that it is hard to dislike it. The ending for this movie is one of my personal favourite movie endings of all time. It is pure genius. If you dislike the movie, fine, I disagree with you heavily but fine. But if you think that ending is stupid, I actually hate you.My one and really only flaw with this film is with some of the dialogue. As much as I love Christopher Nolan, his dialogue can occasionally be too exposition heavy. I 100% understand it was a necessary evil for this film but I still think it was overused. There are a LOT of characters/actors in this movie so I will be brief on the subject. Leonardo DiCaprio was excellent in this movie as Cobb. Ellen Page was great as Ariande. Joseph Gordon-Levitt was excellent as Arthur. 'You mustn't be afraid to Dream a little bigger, darling!' basically sums up the greatness of Tom Hardy's performance as Eames. Marion Cotillard was great as Mal. Cillian Murphy was great as Fischer, as was Ken Wantanabe as rival Saito. Dileep Rao was good as Yusuf but his role was so minute for me to genuinely pay attention. Every character in this movie served a key role to the story and all of them felt important. Even if people like Yusuf were sidelined for the leads, they still felt like they had a purpose.The cinematography for this movie is amazing and there are countless shots in this film that took my breath away. The editing is also exceptional. The visual and practical effects are literally mind. Hans Zimmer's score in this movie is phenomenal. This movie IS, a technical marvel.It is a complex, riveting journey from minute one and I cannot stress enough how amazing this movie is and how much I recommend it. Please, if you have not, see this movie... but be prepared to pay attention. It is 2 1/2 Hours long but it felt like 90 minutes. It is a technical marvel and I'll rate Inception a flawless rating of 10 Totems out of 10.

main_review: It's a well-blended mix of big-budget action movie and mind-bender. Like The Matrix, but the story is more tangible than abstract. Cobb (DiCaprio) is tasked with raiding a corporate heir's dreams and organically implanting ideas in them. How he arrives at the premise of helping the host conceive is a mystery the viewer will have to figure out. Telling a story about interconnected layers of dreaming at once was a difficult task, but Nolan pulls it off near flawlessly.Some action scenes were great, though others should've been pruned to tighten up the pace. I also feel like there could've been less spoonfeeding dialogue. But at the end of the day, you won't find a movie this ambitious that overall comes together so well.

Reviews: A film to twist your idea of reality with amazing results
main_review: We all know our imagination when used can come up some of the most amazing and wonderful things, things that can bring a smile to our face or even make us cringe in fear, the good thing about using our imagination though is it is us who is using it and in that way it is us who controls exactly what happens, the same thing in our dreams as well. We are the ones who control our dreams if we know how. Leonardo DiCaprio (Basketball Diaries, Titanic) plays Dom Cobb a man who with his partner Arthur played by Joseph Gordon Levitt (Mysterious Skin, Stop-Loss) are "extractors", people who can enter the dreams and sub conscious of the unwilling through some military experiment and gather information with their contract none the wiser. The duo is hired by Japanese business man Saito played by Ken Watanabe ( Memoirs of a Geisha, Batman Begins) to enter the sub conscious of Robert Fischer Jr played by Cillian Murphy (Batman Begins, Breakfast on Pluto) and get him to dissolve his dead father's company. If Cobb and his team are successful Saito will ensure the murder charge that Cobb is currently being hunted for (murdering his wife) is dropped and he can go back and be with his two kids once again. Cobb assembles a team ready to enter the 3 levels of Roberts's subconscious whilst he travels from Sydney to Los Angeles with the corpse of his father Inception is a film that if you look away for a second you are utterly lost, miss that one important sentence and you'll be left scratching your head wondering what the hell is actually going on. Is it a film that can hold your attention for the entirety or do you lose interest here and there and wonder what to buy in the supermarket once you leave the cinema? For me it was amazing, so far-fetched and over convoluted, so much bullshit and crazy ideas, so much imagination and wonder all in one very messy and crisscrossed package. I have seen this movie about 3 times now and it still confuses me, in saying that though I do still love it as well. Every time I have watched it I have gotten more and more out of it. I believe it to be the type of film where if two people sitting in the same cinema met after the film to have a coffee and debrief neither of them would agree on the same thing to which they had just seen anyway, both of them would have seen exactly the same thing but come to two very different conclusions. I believe personally that's exactly what Nolan wants from his audience with this film, he wants us (the audience) to walk away and tell each other our own ideas and theories and walk away totally bewildered. For that it works and it works so very well. The scenes set up in some of this movie are beyond imagination, there is one very amazing scene with Joseph Gordon Levitt's character that gives me tingles just thinking about it. Nolan is a very very smart man and no doubt has very big things to bring to the cinematic world. The ending by far is one of the most significant in the film I have my own ideas as I'm sure you will as well. I don't believe this is a film you would enjoy with anyone under 18 and then again even those over 18 without imagination and the ability to escape into a reality of complete amazement won't enjoy it either. Inception gets 4.5 BanShee Screams out of 5 only because there is still so much to it I want to understand and can't without getting Christopher Nolan to sit down and break it down for me even though I'm aware of how much that will kill the entire film for me.

main_review: Is this life? If everything is realistic, what is fake? Am I, in a dream? However, there is rarely dialogue so it isn't a problem. * Dicaprio, Page, and Cotillard star as the main three characters of the film and all three of them give excellent performances.Page's dream sequence in the early portion of the movie is fascinating and I wish they spent more time dwelling on what can happen in a dream than go quickly into the action in the later sequences.The plot thickens, almost a bit too much and then it goes back to the guns and explosions seen in a blockbuster. It somewhat relies a bit too heavily on these guns in the next dream sequence but thankfully it goes back to the plot. I won't say much more as I don't want to spoil anything. Skilled thief DiCaprio gets what he needs by infiltrating his targets' subconscious. DiCaprio leads a cast of fellow young A-listers, and the actors don't crowd each other even though a lot of the characters don't actually have to be there (hush, hush; we'll pretend JGL actually serves a purpose here just because he's so cool). In Nolan we (continue to) trust even when it comes to sci-fi.***½ (out of four)

It takes a highly creative mind to consistently keep thinking out- of-the-box. It takes a compelling story-teller to make you comprehend those thoughts. And it takes a lot of hard-work, dedication and perseverance to convert that story to reel. Put it all together and you have a gist of what went into creating "Inception". And the results speak for themselves!A seamless, "many-layered" film, "Inception" is on one hand a dazzling extravaganza of Science and Technology and on the other, an emotional drama, with the internal conflicts of the lead characters threading through the scenes and binding the entire plot together.This film is no exception to Nolan's unique ability of non-linear story-telling, and it takes a little getting used to. However, once you have an idea of what's going on, you cannot help but marvel at the grandeur and brilliance of it all.Leonardo DiCaprio excelled as the highly-talented but incapacitated mastermind of the group. Ellen Page was right up to the mark playing the young, fresh and at times irritatingly inquisitive "newbie" of the group. Tom Hardy and Joseph Gordon-Levitt's on-screen chemistry was fun to watch. Marion Cotillard and Cilian Murphy had more or less one-dimensional roles to play and they played them okay.Overall, "Inception" is definitely worth watching, and then watching again, and again. It will make you ponder deeper about the realms of the human mind in all senses of the phrase. True to its name, this is a real "inception" of Nolan's and has the power to change the way we think.

t's said that Christopher Nolan spent ten years writing his screenplay for "Inception." That must have involved prodigious concentration, like playing blindfold chess while walking a tight-wire. The film's hero tests a young architect by challenging her to create a maze, and Nolan tests us with his own dazzling maze. We have to trust him that he can lead us through, because much of the time we're lost and disoriented. Nolan must have rewritten this story time and again, finding that every change had a ripple effect down through the whole fabric.Like the hero of that film, the viewer of "Inception" is adrift in time and experience. We can never even be quite sure what the relationship between dream time and real time is. The hero explains that you can never remember the beginning of a dream, and that dreams that seem to cover hours may only last a short time. Yes, but you don't know that when you're dreaming. And what if you're inside another man's dream? How does your dream time synch with his? What do you really know?

Still, in one of my latest revisits, the movie continues to grab my full attention whether it's with smartly written dialog or exciting action scenes. Plus I still believe that DiCaprio deserved a bit more recognition in his role as it's one of great emotional depth.So in Inception we are introduced to a world in which dream-sharing is possible and procedures like extraction are the norm in the espionage game. Cobb (DiCaprio) seems to be the biggest player, but now he is faced with a choice, as a wealthy energy mogul named Saito (Watanabe) promises him an opportunity to stop running and go back home to the U.S. The catch? He must perform Inception on the subject, or in more known terms, implant an idea in the subconscious. Christopher Nolan has directed one the best movies of the genre for me. A complex idea that is shown to the audience by fantastic visuals and asks some pertinent questions, Inception allows you to be entertained but also mentally aware of what's going on. It is a blockbuster movie, there's no question there. However it's one that offers a unique story that plays out at a fast pace and with ideas that will certainly be discussed after the movie finishes.Inception is without a doubt still a great movie. It's been 4 years since its release, so understandably the hype has died down, as has the discussion of the movie's plot. Some of us still love it, others have been let down in repeat viewings, while some still claim the movie is flawed and not smart. Personally I believe it's a masterpiece within the genre. As a general movie? Well that's a discussion for another time. My final advice is whether you end up liking it not, do yourself a favor and watch this movie if you still haven't. It's unmissable.Rating: 10/10

Reviews: Your mind is the scene of crime?
main_review: Nolan attained cult status in Hollywood owing to his master screenplay and narrative in movies like Memento(2002). And his vision of the Batman series was a spectacle that both the fans and non-fans of the series' enjoyed alike. Now Nolan through his imagination has brought us a journey into the world of imagination itself. Inception is about the world of the dream and how to hack into your dreams as well as others. Central to the plot is a piece of tech, developed by the army, which enables people to share dreams. This is what Cobb(Dicaprio) and his associates use to commit mental heists. Cobb lands a job that needs him, not to steal an idea from someone's mind, but to place one there instead and make it seem self-generated by the subject himself. You can do that? This has never been done before but Cobb needs to do this to get back to his children.This movie is not of the sit-back, relax and enjoy genre. It is fast paced and does not wait for you to understand what just happened. Unless you are totally alert, you will get lost. You have to keep track of dreams within dreams and it is not abundantly clear how things actually work in the dream world. But the ten years that Nolan has supposedly put into the film definitely paid off. He masterfully communicates his vision with the audience. The plot has a lot of gaps which the viewer himself has to fill to make the narrative congruent. So this is definitely going to stay on your mind for a while even after you leave the theater. The movie is visually stunning. The CG is seamless and top notch. All the actors render laudable performances. My favorite definitely though is Eames(Tom Hardy). He is a professional thief and an expert forger and extremely cool. But Nolan is no expert at directing fight scenes. They do tend to wear you out as they are not very exciting in themselves. The movie definitely has quite a number of inconsistencies too. This surely must have been due to the short window of time in which Nolan had to present everything about this new world from conception to conclusion. All in all this is a must watch for people who want to challenge their intellect. And as I've said before this not for one's with a faint heart as you might find yourself bored or completely confused unless you are extremely alert.

main_review: Inception. What a masterpiece. Christopher Nolan has really outdone himself with this insane concept of people sharing the same dream space and exploring the idea of a 'dream within a dream'. With Leonardo DiCaprio as the protagonist, Cobb, he puts on a stunning performance, which leaves you speechless and in absolute awe of his uncanny film talent.The movie uses layers of dreams to build up the structure of the movie's plot line, transitioning between each one at alternate stages. With the idea being somewhat unrealistic, the film easily makes up for this through attracting viewers by ensuring that they are eager to uncover the mystery of its non-linear plot line.DiCaprio has a unique acting style that he commonly uses in all of his movies. Throughout Inception though, he slotted comfortably into the life of Cobb and conveyed his life both outstandingly and consistently. The way he expresses pain and emotional difficulties is very believable and he connects with the audiences while doing so. Nolan has put in an exceptional effort in the construction of his film. I recommend it over most films of its genre but to properly gain the most out of it and to completely understand the plot line, the viewer must be engaged constantly. It is worth seeing it twice, almost three times to grasp its general concept. This film's themes are also quite complex and thus, attract audiences who enjoy such themes. Personally, I would rate this film a solid 10 out of 10 for the exceptional effort put in by Nolan and for the elaboration on the central idea of the film, people sharing the same dream space.

I have always been a fan of sci-fi that investigates "reality" and loved the genre becoming more popular in the late 1990s. Having been a huge fan of Philip K. Dick helps and he was amazing to write those books in the 1950s and beyond. Some of my favorite movies are The 13th Floor, Dark City and The Matrix (1999)---a great year for this trio. Additionally, 12 Monkeys, Source Code, Sliding Doors (light romance sci-fi). I read that Christopher Nolan listed his influences for Inception being Paprika and others. When I saw the movie I found shades of Philip K. Dick's The Minority Report (1956) and the anthropology fiction series by Carlos Castenada which began in 1968. The Teachings of Don Juan: A Yaqui Way of Knowledge; A Separate Reality ; and Journey to Ixtlan (1972). These books dealt with different levels of reality, controlled dreaming, etc. Now with AI on the horizon and chatter about reaching "singularity"---I wish I was younger again ( like the characters in Inception --Cobb and Saito.) I would also recommend the 2012 movie Cloud Atlas as an adjunct to this genre. Cloud Atlas, unlike Inception, comes from a book which is a true summer read. 544 pages, which I read---half of War and Peace---the long-standing book length joke.

main_review: Christopher Nolan is one of those few directors that is insanely talented. He just has a knack for making grade A movies and "Inception" was yet another one.In a time and place where it is possible for individuals to enter other people's dreams (ala "Dreamscape" 1984), Cobb (Leonardo DiCaprio) and Arthur (Joseph Gordon-Levitt) do it in order to extract information from people. It's not exactly easy, but then it's better than using violence.The two of them were hired by Saito (Ken Watanabe) to do an inception. That is: they were hired to plant an idea into the subconscious of a slumbering person. In this case the person was a business rival of Saito named Robert Fischer (Cillian Murphy).If extracting information from a dreaming person was hard, planting an idea was exponentially more difficult."Inception" reeled me in with the concept. I was utterly fascinated by the idea. All that remained was to put together a captivating and cohesive movie around that concept, and Nolan did that. It was a beautiful blend of brilliant acting, awesome visual effects, and a solid story. It had to be the best movie of 2010 and a spectacular way to begin the 2010's.

Reviews: A Modern classic that redefines reality
main_review: Christopher Nolan's Inception is nothing short of a cinematic triumph, a film that doesn't just entertain, but challenges its audience on an intellectual level. Combining high-concept science fiction with emotional depth, it's easily one of the most remarkable works of the 21st century.Leonardo DiCaprio delivers one of his strongest performances as Dom Cobb, a skilled extractor navigating the blurry line between dreams and reality. The supporting cast, including Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Marion Cotillard, Ellen Page, and Tom Hardy, adds richness and complexity to an already compelling narrative.But where Inception truly shines is in its technical execution. The visual effects and cinematography are jaw-dropping, seamlessly blending practical effects with CGI in a way that feels both grounded and otherworldly. Hans Zimmer's haunting score elevates every moment.More than a film, Inception is an experience, one that lingers long after the credits roll. It's already a modern classic and a benchmark for sci-fi storytelling.

Christopher Nolan's Inception is one cinematic marvel that pushes the boundaries of filmmaking with its ambition alone. This 2010 creation sees the audacious filmmaker tackle an unprecedented premise, the infiltration, manipulation and weaponizing of dreams. For Nolan, the dreamworld is layered with intricate architecture that can be designed & navigated, and one whose secrets can be plundered. This concept is so original & creative in mind-blowing proportions, that its showcase has audiences hooked with intrigue alone.Apart from its heady premise, Inception as well demands to be celebrated as it is a landmark for technical marvel. For instance, the visual effects that ushers seriously eye-popping imageries such as bending cityscapes deserves applause. The practical effects & camerawork that produced the gravity-defying action sequences in Arthur's dreamworld was jaw dropping in terms of ingenuity & sense of realism, amidst its fantastical beats. As for Inception's sound design, Hans Zimmer's masterful touch simply immerses. His favored usage of booming, relentless rhythms absolutely amplifies the picture's sense of urgency, tension & bewildering feats, essential to Nolan's super grande, dream-bending heist.Coming to Inception's weaknesses, Nolan does stumble when the screenplay becomes exposition-heavy, specially in its attempts to make sense of each & every concept. The interactions can then feel mechanical, and with an obvious lack of transcendent performances from its ensemble, the dialogue can feel weightless and jargon-steeped. The emotional core of the film however more than makes up, as the storyline that revolves around Cobb's guilt & yearning for Mal was deeply affecting, with emotionally-provoking twists to boot.Overall, Nolan once again proves his impressive cinematic artistry, that delivers movies that dazzle the eyes and electrifies the mind. Inception is EXACTLY this, an innovative blockbuster that tackles the undiscovered, showcasing its tenets with hypnotizing images. It is really an amazing film to experience!

Reviews: A mind-bending masterpiece - smart, stylish, and utterly unforgettable
main_review: Christopher Nolan's Inception is a landmark in modern cinema - an ambitious, cerebral thriller that challenges its audience to keep up and rewards them with one of the most original and exhilarating cinematic experiences in decades.The film follows Dom Cobb (Leonardo DiCaprio), a skilled thief who specializes in extracting secrets from dreams. But his latest mission flips the concept: instead of stealing an idea, he must plant one - a process known as inception. What unfolds is a layered, visually stunning journey through dreams within dreams, blurring the line between reality and illusion.Nolan masterfully balances complex concepts with heart-pounding action, aided by a stellar cast (Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Ellen Page, Tom Hardy, Marion Cotillard) and Hans Zimmer's iconic, thunderous score. The "hallway fight" scene? Pure cinematic brilliance. The spinning top? Legendary.At its core, Inception isn't just about dreams - it's about guilt, grief, and the human mind's desire for control and escape. It's intellectually dense but emotionally grounded, and despite all the complexity, it never loses sight of its characters.Inception is the kind of film that lingers in your mind long after the credits roll - twisting, unraveling, and daring you to dive back in.

I watched a movie that was so exciting and mind-opening that it marked the last 10 years of science fiction-action cinema: InceptionIn fact, this is not the first time that an idea has been implemented in Inception! If you take the '60s "team movies" template and insert into it the idea of a sci-fi theft of stealing ideas by navigating through layers of dreams, this story emerges. But if there is a director like Christopher Nolan, one of the last great storytellers, who has long ago come of age for friend and foe, who sent the bearded brothers (Spielberg, Lucas) to the Memories 9 album , the result is a must-see film even in the July heat when Turkish people refrain from going to the cinema.The beginning tells the story of a team of idea players, all of whom are experts in their business, together with a fledgling but promising dream builder who joins them, this time trying to collapse a company that is taking giant steps towards monopolization by injecting ideas instead of stealing ideas, but what to tell... This is a great visual labyrinth of 148 minutes, where the action and tension that starts from a high point increases and you will watch by biting your nails...Christopher Nolan wrote his screenplay on the assumption that the audience wasn't retarded, unlike popular Hollywood screenwriters, who can't be put on the ground, but I'd hesitate to even write an elementary school play, and he did it well. While American TV is flooded with a plethora of clever series, North American cinema, which has become increasingly silly and turned into amusement park entertainment, is in dire need of such touches. I admit that the escalating action makes it a little difficult to understand the plot as our heroes descend to a lower level in the dream layers, but Nolan's top-notch direction simplifies everything on the way to the finale and allows you to come out of the movie with clarity and full of the story. Ideas such as "time differentiations between dream layers" and "totems that create awareness" made the film much more delicious.Di Caprio, who has escaped the curse of being a baby-faced character actor due to his advancing age, plays comfortably and convincingly from the hallucinations of Dungeon Island. Among the actors who accompanied her, the first ones to appear were Ellen Page, whom we know from Juno, and the Japanese actor Ken Vatanabe, whom I admire very much. Cillian Murphy, Batman Begins' "Scarecrow", brings the character of businessman Robert Fischer to life in a more successful Nolan movie.Perhaps what a science fiction movie needs most is visual effects... This is where Double Negative and Plowman Craven & Associates come in and do a clean and believable job that doesn't look like the work of ILM or Zeta, but doesn't sacrifice the film to CGI either. The dream world sequences created by the protagonist Cobb, played by Leonardo Di Caprio, and his wife Mal are especially worth seeing.Hans Zimmer is a musical genius who I believe is not out of this world, and I believe that "good movies have good music..." In accordance with the rule, he has created a soundtrack work that surpasses even my favorite work, Gladiator.

A wildly creative high-concept action-packed thriller that starts off hazy with its complications, but quickly wins you over once the fog dies down and everything begins to make sense. It's much like riding a roller coaster at night: you may not always know what's going on, but you're still having a fun time with the sheer absurdity of the situation that's been expertly handcrafted just for your entertainment. The main cast are all terrific and bounce off each other really well despite some tropey rocky starts at the beginning. The plot keeps on hooking you into its narrative with its creative visual set pieces that explore some pretty interesting and profound concepts about dreams, escapism, coping with grief, memory, re-memory, psychosis, and the subconscious. Despite all the memes and pale imitators, Hans Zimmers' score is still amazing with its thrilling booming sense of urgency, with the trailer music being my favorite track despite not making an appearance in the movie itself. The set design and shift camera work are amazing and really lull the viewer into a dream-like state, much like the protagonists of the film. Mad props to the cast for being able to convincingly work off each other across different dream scenarios that are seamlessly edited to appear simultaneously. After all these years, I finally get why everyone was freaking out about the spinning top at the very end of the movie. It may give you a bit of a headache by the end, but Inception will give you more than enough cinematic creativity, gripping character drama, and intriguing philosophy to make you more than satisfied.
